[spoiler=[b][pre]The War on Opium[/pre][/b]

[i][b][pre]Sunder them, and return their pieces to me.
~Sealiph Ibrahim[/pre][/b][/i]]

Ever since the capitulation of the Sybu Republic in 2003, Irocco has been engaged in an asymmetric conflict against the Maiqah Opium Cartel, which occupies the highlands surrounding the territories annexed by the Sealiphate following their victory after the 2002 Irocco-Sybuic Continuation War. Several thousand soldiers of the Itiammudian Islamic Army have been tied up fighting in the mountains alongside the local Maiqah Defence Forces, who are a confederated group of various Maiqah organisations and former veterans attempting to survive in the post-Emirate of Maiqahstan collapse world while not being put under the thumb of drug runners. 

The Itiammudian Islamic Army has been partially engaged in the conflict since 2003, though until 2024, there was only limited support of the Maiqah Defence Forces, with the greatest extent of Iroccoan support being a handful of soldiers. However, since 2024, Iroccoan involvement has spiked with the Consultative Assembly of Iyaiids pushing Sealiph Ibrahim to commit further into the Maiqah conflict to stabilise the al-Sybu frontier, break the opium trade into Irocco and, secretly but obviously, to those who knew about the economy of the now fallen Maiqah Emirate, secure the natural gas reserves under the control of the Opium Cartel.

For the past three years, Iroccoan involvement in the conflict has been slowly but surely creeping up; a total of two divisions of the Itiammudian Islamic Army (Ground Forces) and several aircraft have been committed to the Maiqah Defence Force. Villages outside of the sway of both the Maiqah Defence Force and the Opium Cartel have been put under the direct protection of Irocco. It was clear to outside observers that Irocco might be gearing up for the annexation of Maiqah. It was denied by the Iroccoan Government officially, but unofficially, the Consultative Assembly of Iyaiids have pushed for total annexation.

By September of 1449 (Hijiri) or 2027 in the Gregorian calendar, Irocco had set the stage to sweep into Maiqahstan and secure both its borders and a reserve of natural gas. Iroccoan-aligned village chiefs had been primed by Iroccoan agents to proclaim their desire to be annexed into Irocco following the fall of the Opium Cartel. While some elements of the Maiqah Defence Forces might be against their annexation, several elements are determined to be in favour, such as the Maiqah Mujahidin who adhere to Itiammudian Islam. It is predicted by the Iroccoan Government that a plurality of those inside the region of Maiqahstan will accept annexation.

-

Lieutenant Qasim Nahw of the 3rd Islamic Platoon under the 2nd deployed Islamic Division sent to fight in Maiqahstan under Sealiph Ibrahim's renewed attempt to secure Maiqahstan enters into the public school currently occupied by the Itiammudian Islamic Army by the grace of the local chief to serve as housing. He inspects the surprisingly well-kept state of the school despite the several weeks of Iroccoan occupation. 

He walks through the halls, taking stock of their current situation and supplies when he gets a whiff of it, kicking up dust, diesel and choking smoke that blacks out the skies. A Cartel assault group is coming; their inefficient gas-guzzling trucks crawl down the cracked roads towards the village. Lieutenant Qasim turns around and breaks into a sprint, unholstering his PC-9 Zoaf, shouting to his men outside, begging anyone to ring the bell, a sign for the locals to hide and his men to rally. 
 
His cries are not in vain; the bell tolls outside, and he hears the scrambling of feet outside and the shouts of disciplined Mubarizun-like soldiers. Lieutenant Qasim kicks open the door and turns toward the road. They neared closer and closer. But he had a moment to retrieve his AK-74M; he would reach it just before the Cartel arrived. 

Their initial assault bore down hard, but they had been fighting for so long that their weapons were severely out of date, and their bullets were in short supply. Lieutenant Qasim ordered his platoon to hold until they needed to reload, then the retaliation came. The 3rd Islamic Platoon showed their strength as they responded in kind. Three Iroccoans died in the Cartel's initial attack for thirteen killed in the Iroccoan response. 

A detachment of the Platoon was sent to flank the Cartel convoy. They climbed over the hills and back around the road. They pointed their guns at the Cartel grunts' exposed backs and shouted in Shamatine for their surrender. In a broken version of Gods tongue, they responded, throwing down their weapons and raising their hands, surrendering to the Iroccoans. 

Under Iroccoan pressure, they broke, words spilt forth from their immoral mouths about the massing of resources and manpower to begin an assault on the main Maiqah Defence Force headquarters. The collective Cartel Families had noticed the increased Iroccoan presence and determined that a full intervention might be on the way. If the Maiqah Defence Force can be shattered before that comes to pass, then perhaps they can secure Maiqahstan for themselves and dig in to hold against a future Iroccoan assault and continue the Opium trade for their collective profit. 

The Great Cartel Attack is planned for the 23rd of September; the city of Ryhdi must hold. Lieutenant Qasim made contact with the home base back in Irocco. He informed command of the imminent assault on their allies. 

-

The young operator named Ayman sat in his office seat waiting for contact from anyone in Maiqahstan. It was a boring duty at the best of times and a heart-attack-causing stress at the worst of times. His headset crackled as he answered his most recent call. 3rd Platoon Lieutenant Qasim Nahw speaking, I have information for Homebase over, Ayman replied. Hearing you loud and clear, patching you through now over.

He overheard the conversation between his betters in Homebase and the soldiers on the front. Lieutenant Qasim Nahw speaking, I have Cartel grunts here talking about some upcoming assault on Ryhdi. Info seems good, could be a diversion though. It's scheduled for the 23rd. 

Heard, Ill pass the information up the chain of command. Well figure it out from there. Continue current operations, attempt to secure support from your host.

Heard clear.

Click.

-

Lieutenant Qasim picked his ear and flicked wax from it onto the floor. He would begin to make his way towards the village chief. Discussions to bring him onside had been ongoing for some time but had been reasonably unsuccessful. Perhaps with the defence of his village and the coming news of a renewed Cartel assault, the possibility of victory might convince the stubborn old goat to yield.

He would make his way up the hill towards the modest house of the Chief. It looked as if it was carved from the very hill it topped. Lieutenant Qasim respected the old man, though he disagreed with his lack of agreement with the Iroccoan vision for Maiqahstan. 

Lifting up the heavy fabric, Lieutenant Qasim entered the house. As-salamu alaykum. Spoke the tired voice from the corner of the room. Wa-Alaikum-Salaam, I have returned to your home to discuss the matter once more. Replied the comparatively youthful voice.

As expected, come then. The tea is brewed. He gestured Qasim further into his home and offered him a seat on the floor.

The tea was poured, first for Qasim and then for himself.

Convince me again, not from some rehearsed script, but from your heart.

Qasim was taken aback but responded as the man wished. The Sealiphate is a nation that has built a strong foundation for its people and for the people of al-Sybu, despite the constant attempts of the Sybic Government to bring Irocco under its heel. If Sealiph Ibrahim would not repress them, why would he repress your nation? For the security of Irocco and for Maiqahistan, it must be brought into the fold lest further chaos occur in the absence of a ruling government. Things will change little for your people; you will still hold sway over this town. Your culture will be respected; the only difference is no drugs and a different man to pay taxes to.

The old man was surprised, mildly surprised, but surprised nonetheless. He had not expected such an answer after hearing the regular dribble. Surprising to hear wise words coming from such a young man; however, how could you hold your government to such statements?

Because proof of such has already been given. As I said, Sybic remains respected, while they are not as numerous as the Iroccoans, they have not been Iroccoanised. Their unique way of life is preserved under the Sealiphate. If that is not assurance enough, I do not know what is.

The chief nodded. I relent, you have protected my people and offered truth. We have drunk tea under the same roof, respect to you, commander of war.

Qasim smiled; his own father had died some time ago, and the words of the old man had brought a mite of fatherly respect. He thanked the old man and departed from him. He ordered a skeleton crew of defenders to remain in the village as he and the remainder of the soldiers moved to join the rest of the Itiammudian Islamic Army as they prepared for the defence of Ryhdi.

-

The golden eagle soars above the skies of the mountains compound of the Dharic Family, a part of the much larger Maiqah Cartel, which has been in an ongoing battle against the Maiqah Defence Forces, which is itself several groups working as one, and the Itiammudian Islamic Army of Irocco. The Cartel is long past its territorial prime, though the opium it is pushing remains highly lucrative. The head of the Uraik family, known as al-Upran, is looking over his closest lieutenants in an all-too-tight meeting room.

 Let's get our facts straight, the Cartel Council has fvcked us over with this idiotic fvcking assault plan. We are not helping those bastards, we are not throwing away decades of work for a chance to restore a pipedream, were pulling out of Maiqahstan into Irocco and out again before we get killed by the Police, or Haras, or Army or any number of groups that can execute us. Were getting as much opium and guns out of Maiqahstan onto a ship. Put out feelers, I dont plan to sink this boat fulla money, unlike the rest of our organisation.

al-Uprans closest look around at each other, secretly weighing the cost of betrayal against the profit potential of going along with al-Upran. Some debate internally, betraying al-Upran himself, though those thoughts are shot down with a glare. 

While the two titans of the Maiqahstan conflict slug it out in the final battle to determine the fate of the former nation-state, the Uraik prepare a great convoy of trucks packed full of opium, bullets, guns and other narcotics. Iroccoan Inars that flowed into their pockets are also brought to be used along the journey.

While not a major element of the Cartel, the Uraik make up several thousand well-trained fighters, which the Cartel has now lost out on. The flight of the Uraik is a great benefit for the Iroccoan cause in Maiqahstan. 

During their flight, they made contact with several criminal organisations throughout Erene in order to offload the remainder of their goods and guns, perhaps forge a new foothold in a foreign land or simply retire wealthy. Though the calm life is never one for one in the family.

-

In the lead up to the 23rd Sealiph Ibrahim was contacted by forward operating base J-33 15 Eagle, which held the commanders of the Maiqahstan Operation. Ibrahim was contacted over the commencement of Operation Yunus, named for the minor Prophet Yunus (Jonah). The operation was designed as a preemptive strike done by the Haras sent by Ibrahim, followed by the formal main army attack or repulsion from Ryhdi if Operation Yunus failed to cause enough damage to halt the assault.

Ibrahim discussed the plan in depth with Irman the Stern as he knew his men well. It was formally approved by both a few hours after receiving the initial report from forward operating base J-33 15 Eagle. It would commence on the 22nd. 

The Operation itself was a decapitation; its goal was to eliminate the commanding Lieutenants of the upcoming assault on Ryhdi and, if possible, the overall field marshal of the theatre, who is the head of the al-Zhahum Family. The decapitation operation would be under the jurisdiction of Mahar al-Kaham, who would break his force of forty Haras Furusiyya into eight squads of five who would each assault their respective targets.

Five out of eight decapitations were successful, with three failing due to a lack of an opportune moment. The head of the al-Zhahum family was maimed, though he lived. A less experienced al-Zhahum commander was put in charge of the assault, and on the morning of the 23rd, the assault continued as planned, though severely weaker than it would have been otherwise.

-

The Itiammudian Islamic Army occupied the hills and mountains surrounding the city, as the main Cartel assault force pushed into the flat ground between the surrounding mountains and began their artillery shelling of the city, the Iroccoans began to descend upon their flank and open unrelenting fire. A vanguard force of tanks stored away from the city and far away from Cartel sights sprang into action, driving behind the ill-prepared and poorly commanded force of souls who turn from His light.

The Itiammudian Islamic Air Force took off from airbases on the border. HESA Saeqeh light fighters rained down fire from above as they dodged rocket fire from Cartel ground troops who remained untouched by Iroccoan bullets. Cartel Anti-Air trucks also responded by downing one or two HESA Saeqeh light fighters by a miracle of the profane. 

Maiqah fighters poured out from the city and began to attack the front of the Cartel forces. Sandwiching the Opium peddlers between them, they died in the hundreds, Iroccoan armour and manpower proving unstoppable against a fundamentally weaker foe.

Though this abject slaughter would not wholly be one-sided, as the Cartel called in reinforcements, fearing that the inexperienced al-Zhahum commander would botch this vital operation. The head of the al-Zhahum family and the remainder of the Cartels fighting force slammed into the exposed Iroccoan rear, causing terror in their backlines. However, Iroccoan armoured once more proved decisive as it turned and wheeled back to the backline with speed. 2S25 Sprut-SD, being the first to engage, ran over some and destroyed as many Cartel vehicles and anti-tank weaponry as possible before the Karrar Main Battle Tank charged into the fray, causing mass cartel casualties.

The Cartel al-Zhahum Core Division began its last desperate acts, throwing themselves at the Iroccoans, who returned with bullet hell. The Cartel attack would break a few short hours following the opening salvo of Cartel Artillery. 

-

Following the victory and the fall of most of the Cartel forces, the Itiammudian Islamic Army would then be half mobilised and push fully into Maiqahstan, throwing a hundred and twenty thousand men into a full attempt to wipe out any remaining resistance and set up an informal occupation, which would be completed near the end of September. 

Negotiations would remain ongoing with the faux-occupation lasting till November, until Sealiph Ibrahim determined that the locals seemed inclined enough to agree to total annexation under the Black Banner. On the thirteenth of December, a Maiqah-wide election was held, propped up by Irocco and validated by uh someone. Trust us. 

The ballot read the following:

Would you accept total Iroccoan annexation and integration of Maiqahstan?

Yes
No
Abstain

The ballot was sent out to all villages, towns and cities by the Irocccoan authorities garrisoning them. Following the several previous months of Iroccoan good works in Maiqahstan. Such as the rebuilding of the Maiqah industry, crushing the cartels, reintroducing law and order, breaking the back of Opium sales in Maiqahstan and furthermore preserving the Maiqah way of life despite blatant occupation, elected to vote in favour with a majority of 78% voting in favour of annexation, 12% abstaining, and the remainder denying. 

By the fifteenth of December, Iroccoan maps were redrawn to include Maiqahstan and its newly drawn Mintaqahs, which largely followed local chief influence who would be declared Emirs by Sealiph Ibrahim in the Maiqah Crowning Edict. While Irocco attempted to preserve the Maiqah way of life, those Chiefs who voted against integration were replaced, as is righteous under Iroccoan law. 

-

Sealiph Ibrahim would make a speech on the new unity. The following is an extract of that speech; it would continue for some time after reiterating the points made within.

...Praise be to Allah and the martyrs of Islam, for this day Dar al-Islam grows more unified, and the house of Shaytan, the secularists, the disbelievers and apostates lose out on another state. The Mizrahelic entity loses out on a weakened and fractured state to influence and contort to serve Baal, as is the nature of the Mizrahellionic spawn. The unity of Sybu with Irocco was a great step forward, and now, most joyously, Maiqahstan has joined in this greatness. Though the circumstances of unity under the Trustee of God, the Sealiph, is a sad one for we had many dead to bring about and bring about the destruction of the Opium trade within Irocco, joy still abounds.

The Cartel, led astray by the whispers of Shaytan in hope of profit instead of the Prophets were fools, they will serve in halls of the suffering in Jahannam, and they will beg the Almighty for another chance, but alas this Dunya is a test and they have spent their test in pursuit of worldly things instead of submission to the will of Allah, his divine laws as set forth by the Noble Quran and interpreted by my tribe as he decreed following the rise of the false Caliphates of Umayyi. Indeed, all praise is due to Him who knows what we will do and how we will fail Him, but allows our repentance and is forgiving so long as we know Him, and He knows us through our submission.

But alas, the Cartel knew this not, or perhaps they did and yet ignored the warning signs. Despite these most mournful acts, we praise Him and give due respect to the Martyrs of Unity as we bring Maiqahstan into the fold of the Iron Sealiphate

Following this speech, the Maiqah Crowning Edict would be made, and Maiqahstan would be formally integrated into Irocco, forevermore.

[/spoiler]

[i]The existence of the Maiqah State has not been a reality for some time, since the fall of the Emirate; they have been suffering under the thumb of the Cartel, which has corrupted their youths and killed thousands in the pursuit of profit. Corrupted hundreds of thousands with the pushing of Opium, for the security of our people, we banded together with Maiqah Defence Forces for the past two decades. Where was New Westmore? The West issues dictates over issues that they can not possibly comprehend, over a culture alien to their own. The Maiqah nation has been in ruins, and though they are not of the Iroccoan Culture, they are of our faith. Nationalism is the great poison of Shaytan over this Dunya, though I would not expect you to understand. The Maiqah people themselves, through plebiscite, decided to leave aside the slave-bondage of nationalism and join the Sealiphate, though we use the name Irocco, I would have it burnt if I could, if that was what was required for the return of a greater Islamic entity. The Government of Greater Tirakan confirms the arrival and operational integration of new military equipment, notable Dhoran air-defense such as the recently delivered 96K6-SM units. These systems are now undergoing training phases within Tirakan.

Furthermore, Tirakans first-line allies and defensive partners, [nation]Vespurias[/nation], [nation]Valddera[/nation], [nation]Imazighen Emirates[/nation], and [nation]Newer Hydronia[/nation], have been called to take part in the upcoming annual combined military exercises. Separately, the government announces in a recent Communiqué that its review of the national economy has been concluded. The assessment confirms that Greater Tirakan possesses the logistical, industrial and financial capacity and reserves to sustain a temporary war-economy posture if required, without systemic disruption.
This is not a declaration of intent, but a warning to challenging enemies.
Yet Tirakan continues to prefer stability. But do not mistake, as peace does not come easy.

[Spoiler=[b][U]Il-76 Special Delivery[/u][/b]]

The hum of the engines was heard long before the aircraft was seen. The Dhora Il-76 broke through the morning mist and touched down with a thunderous thud. In the next hour, all three Il-76s would land in a Tirakan airbase, all painted in the same signature grey.

The Dhora officers directed the Tirakan servicemen as they offloaded its cargo. The first plane carried four P-18-2 early warning radars, digital solid-state versions of the faithful P-18 that had served Dhora SAM teams well across decades. The second had an endless array of crates. Spare parts for the newly delivered P‑18s and Pantsirs. The third carried pallets of ammunition: missiles sealed in protective canisters and belts of autocannon rounds.

Alongside the equipment was a delegation of Dhora officers. These were veterans, SAM teams that had operated their equipment for at least a decade, and here to train Tirakan's officers in operating the Pantsirs and P-18s.[/spoiler]

[Spoiler=[b][u]Training[/u][/b]]

Colonel Hussein and his lieutenants stand in front of the assembled Tirakan SAM teams. Around them are the P-18 radars and Pantsirs he's there to train them to become proficient in.

"Soldiers, we, as SAM teams, are the least thought of part of the military. We get the least respect in peacetime and then have to pull miracles in war to keep the skies clear and our armed forces safe. You'll, overtime, come to realise that your superiors are often uninformed about the correct way to use SAM systems. In Dhornaper, the generals keep out of our way and let us at the brigade level handle stuff ourselves. Your military may be different...

...

Contrary to official Dhora doctrine, none of our SAM teams fire from the maximum range of the SAM systems for two reasons:

[List=1]
[*]From maximum range, the enemy has the easiest chance of escaping your engagement envelope. You want to hug their belt as much as possible, fire from sub-20km ranges to deny them escape.
[*]From maximum range, you must illuminate the enemy much longer with your fire control radar. The longer you illuminate, the more likely you are to be hit with an anti-radiation missile. Keep all radar emissions to under 20 seconds. Radiating for less than 20 seconds will prevent an anti-radiation missile from being able to exactly determine your location, increasing the chances that it will miss your equipment.
[/list]

...

After every illumination and missile launch, you must relocate to a new location. Treat your old location as compromised.

...

Always illuminate with your radar imitators at the same time to reduce the likelihood of being hit with an anti-radiation missile. Imitators are cheap and expendable.

...

Camouflage your equipment and create decoys so optical observers cannot see your real equipment, and hit your decoy equipment. We have supplied you with inflatable decoys, use them wisely.

...

After every engagement, report to command with the details of what happened, how, and why. Your reports will help train your comrades from your experience.

...

You must maintain three levels of readiness:

[List=1]
[*]Readiness Level 1 is when your team is at their stations and ready to engage immediately.
[*]Readiness Level 2 is when your team is at their stations but the equipment is off. Still, your team should be able to switch to Readiness Level 1 at a moments notice.
[*]Readiness Level 3 is when your team is ready to enter Readiness Level 1 within ten minutes. You do not have to be at your stations for this.
[/list]

Any readiness worse than Readiness Level 3 is unacceptable.

...

Your P-18 is an early warning radar. It can detect aircraft at up to 360km in ideal circumstances. Circumstances are, of course, never ideal. It is too inaccurate to guide your missiles. Since it uses an extremely long wavelength, it will not be detected by the enemy, nor will it be targeted by anti-radiation missiles. Still, usage should be minimal to lower maintenance requirements.

When an enemy aircraft is detected on the P-18, it will appear as a round circle. You will get approximate direction and range for it. You then must use your Pantsir acquisition radar to get the altitude of the targe and the exact range and direction from which you can fire your missiles. Remember, never use the acquisition radar for more than 20 seconds and never at ranges longer than 20km.

...

Stealth technology is not invisible. Your P-18 will detect stealth aircraft at ranges of up to 100km. Your Pantsir acquisition radar will acquire them at closer than 20km just fine.

...

Towed decoys can fool your teams. Over time, you will become experienced enough to notice decoys. A key giveaway is that your radar will see two targets at the same altitude and going in the same direction. The fainter one is typically the real aircraft. The one that appears to be trailing the other is always the decoy. You will learn to distinguish them in time.

...

Jammers are a unique threat. They will prevent your acquisition radar from working. The Pantsirs have a counter to this: it is called passive angle tracking.
